en.name: Catherine of Genoa
en.summary: Italian noblewoman who, after a sudden conversion, devoted decades to nursing plague victims and writing on purgatory.
en.body: Catherine was married off at sixteen to a Genoese nobleman in an unhappy, loveless marriage, and spent a decade in worldly distraction before an abrupt spiritual conversion during confession left her, by her own account, overwhelmed with divine love and shame for her past life. She subsequently reformed her difficult husband, who joined her in penitential living, and together they moved into Genoa's largest hospital, where she eventually became director and personally nursed patients through repeated outbreaks of plague, contracting the disease herself at least once. Her recorded spiritual conversations and reflections, compiled after her death by her followers, include an influential treatise on purgatory describing it as a purifying encounter with God's love rather than mere punishment, which shaped later Catholic thought on the subject. She died in 1510 and was canonized in 1737.
